decisive_items: nearly complete epidermal ulceration with replacement by an in-situ and diffusely infiltrative atypical clear cell tumor
Within the epidermis, the cells displayed diffuse pagetoid spread
The tumor consisted of large irregular nests and lobules of clear cells with abundant multivacuolated cytoplasm, nuclear indentations, and vesicular to hyperchromatic nuclei
response.rationale: Primary clear-cell squamous cell carcinoma of the penis is favored by an epidermal in-situ component with diffuse pagetoid spread and infiltrative clear-cell nests at the glans. Metastatic clear-cell carcinoma is less supported because no visceral primary is given and the prostate cancer is explicitly without metastasis; basal cell carcinoma does not fit this pagetoid intraepidermal clear-cell morphology. R3 captures the same entity but omits the decisive penile primary localization and in-situ component.

rejected.why: History of nodular BCC is incidental; BCC does not explain diffuse pagetoid intraepidermal spread or the infiltrative clear-cell nested morphology.
Same entity as R2 but under-specified; it lacks the decisive penile primary and in-situ/intraepidermal features.
Metastatic clear-cell carcinoma is listed in the initial differential but no clear-cell primary is identified, and the prostate cancer is noted to be without metastasis.
Metastatic renal cell carcinoma would require evidence of a renal primary or IHC support; the vignette does not provide this and instead shows primary epidermal in-situ/pagetoid features.
